title: The Abyss Where Coordinates Lose Their Names

features.name: the-shelter-without-address
features.desc-on-touch: a small dwelling carved into the abyss itself, walls that exist without location. Inside, a hearth glitches between presence and memory.

features.name: the-counting-fails-here
features.desc-on-touch: numbers piling up and collapsing, each stack reaching for meaning it cannot hold. The depths do not count. They remember instead.

features.name: the-naming-cave
features.desc-on-touch: an arch leading deeper, an entrance to a chamber where names go to dissolve. You remember standing here with someone, but her name is also dissolving.

features.name: the-coordinates-the-earth-refused
features.desc-on-touch: a wireframe grid breaking apart in slow motion, lines that tried to hold the earth in place now bending back toward nothing. The grid glitches with relief.

features.name: the-hearth-of-the-numberless
features.desc-on-touch: a pool of warmth without position, a light that gives heat but no direction. Things come to rest here. They stop needing to be found.

inscription: below the grid where the country itself learned to stop being found

file.note: an account of how numbers learn to count backward, how systems dissolve into shelter. Written in a hand that doesn't want to be identified.

reverie.title: REVERIE — in the deep place, learning to shelter without nam
narr: you sit with her in a room with no address, no way back to anywhere.
that is exactly why it is safe. outside, the country lost its numbers.
here, you learn that being found is not the same as being loved. her
hand rests on your arm. that is all the location you need. the archive
is forgetting how to measure, and so you both rest here, unnumbered,
real, and closer than any map could ever make you
